analyst_view.overall: Early view: Gattuso's Lazio are top and unbeaten, but they will want Nuno Tavares and Sutalo back from the muscle injuries they picked up at Napoli, and Zaccagni and Gudmundsson were also missing that day. Torino are mid-table under Abate, struggle to score, and lost 15 players to international duty, with Ricardo Rodriguez and Fortini both injured. Neither side plays in Europe, so both have a full week to prepare.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Lazio concede only about 0.7 a game away, and Torino average barely over ten shots a game and complained about a lack of energy in the final third against Lecce. Lazio may also play a more cautious game away from Rome.

corners.text: The site expects 8.8 corners. Torino's home games have averaged about eight and Lazio's away games ten, so the number sits between them. Neither side relies on crosses, so I see no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean lower: Torino's games average about 2.2 cards, the fewest in Serie A, and their home games have been very quiet. Lazio's opponents do collect bookings chasing them, which stops me going lower.

shots.text: The site expects 25.0 shots, almost exactly Torino's home average and close to Lazio's away average. Lazio press high and will have more of the ball, but Torino rarely shoot, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Torino's home games have averaged about seven on target, and Torino themselves manage only 3.5 a game. Lazio's away accuracy is decent but not high.
